examples.en: You need practice in thinking logically.
He is a person who thinks about problems differently.
If you think deeply, the answer shows up.
Children think while they play.
When I thought flexibly, a solution came to mind.
Gather information before you reason it through.

explain: '생각하다'는 일상 말이고, '사고하다'는 논리적으로 따져 생각한다는 딱딱한 글말이에요. 대화에서는 거의 안 쓰고 '사고력', '창의적으로 사고하다'처럼 교육·논문에서 자주 나와요. 소리가 같은 '사고(事故, accident)'와 구별하세요.

phrases.en: There are many students who think creatively.
phrases.nuance_ko: 교육 이야기에서 자주 나오는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Often appears when talking about education.

phrases.en: Reading books improves your thinking ability.
phrases.nuance_ko: '사고하다'에서 나온 말로, 생각하는 힘을 뜻해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Comes from 사고하다 and means the power to think.

phrases.en: Think deeply before you answer.
phrases.nuance_ko: 대화에서는 '사고하다' 대신 '생각하다'를 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: In conversation, use 생각하다 instead of 사고하다.

explain_en: Formal, written: structured, intellectual thinking. '생각하다' is everyday; '사고하다' is a stiff written word for reasoning logically. It's rare in conversation and shows up in education and papers, like '사고력'. Don't mix it up with the same-sounding '사고' (accident).

examples.en: You brought an umbrella ahead of time, what foresight!

examples.ko: 그때 집을 사 둔 건 정말 선견지명이었어요.
examples.en: Buying the house back then was truly a wise move.
He had foresight, so his investment succeeded.

examples.ko: 선견지명이 없었다면 큰 손해를 봤을 거예요.
examples.en: Without that foresight, we would have suffered a big loss.

examples.ko: 사장님의 선견지명 덕분에 회사가 위기를 넘겼어요.
examples.en: Thanks to the boss's foresight, the company got through the crisis.

examples.ko: 저는 선견지명이 부족해서 늘 준비가 늦어요.
examples.en: I lack foresight, so I'm always late preparing.

explain: 보통 '선견지명이 있다/없다'로 쓰고, 미리 준비한 일이 잘됐을 때 '선견지명이네요'라고 칭찬해요. 우산을 챙기는 것 같은 작은 일에도 가볍게 쓸 수 있어요.

phrases.example: 그 사람은 선견지명이 있어서 미리 준비했어요.
phrases.en: He had foresight, so he prepared in advance.
phrases.nuance_ko: 앞일을 미리 내다보는 능력이 있다는 칭찬이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A compliment that someone can see ahead.

phrases.example: 저는 선견지명이 없어서 늘 늦게 준비해요.
phrases.en: I have no foresight, so I always prepare late.
phrases.nuance_ko: 미리 대비하지 못했을 때 아쉬움을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Expresses regret about not preparing ahead.

phrases.en: That investor is famous for his excellent foresight.
phrases.nuance_ko: 능력이 매우 좋다고 높이 평가하는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A strong praise of someone's ability.

explain_en: It is usually used as '선견지명이 있다/없다', and you praise someone with '선견지명이네요' when their early preparation paid off. You can use it lightly even for small things like bringing an umbrella.

examples.ko: 첫인상 때문에 선입관을 갖지 않으려고 해요.
examples.en: I try not to form preconceptions because of first impressions.
Try eating it once without any preconceptions.
My preconception about that person was broken.

examples.ko: 외모만 보고 선입관을 가지면 안 돼요.
examples.en: You shouldn't form preconceptions just by looking at appearance.
I missed a good chance because of my preconception.

examples.ko: 그 영화는 선입관과 달리 정말 재미있었어요.
examples.en: Unlike what I assumed, that movie was really fun.

explain: '편견'은 한쪽으로 치우친 나쁜 생각에 가깝고, '선입관'은 직접 겪기 전에 미리 가진 생각이라 좋은 쪽일 수도 있어요. '선입견'이라고도 하고, '선입관을 갖다/버리다/깨다'처럼 써요.

phrases.en: I misunderstood that person because of a preconception.
phrases.nuance_ko: '선입관'과 거의 같은 뜻이고 둘 다 많이 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Almost the same as 선입관; both are widely used.

phrases.example: 처음 보는 음식에 선입관을 갖지 마세요.
phrases.en: Don't have preconceptions about food you see for the first time.
phrases.nuance_ko: 미리 정해 둔 생각이 있을 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when you already have a fixed idea.

phrases.en: If you drop your preconceptions, you can see new things.
phrases.nuance_ko: 미리 가진 생각을 내려놓는다는 뜻이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Means to put aside what you assumed beforehand.

explain_en: '편견' leans toward a biased, negative view, while '선입관' is an idea formed before experiencing something, which can even be positive. It is also said '선입견', and used as '선입관을 갖다/버리다/깨다'.

examples.en: I want to hold on to even the faintest hope to the end.
The chance of rescue was slim as a thread, so everyone was worried.
The faint expectation finally became reality.
His voice sounded as thin as a thread.
The odds of winning are slim, but I'll give it a try.
I didn't give up even when the possibility was extremely slim.

explain: '희망', '가능성', '목숨'처럼 거의 사라질 듯 아주 약하게 남은 것과 함께 써요. '실낱같은 희망'이라는 덩어리로 외워 두면 편해요.

phrases.en: His life hung by a thread, but we didn't give up.
phrases.nuance_ko: 곧 사라질 듯 아주 약한 생명을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for a life so weak that it may fade at any moment.
phrases.en_equiv: a life hanging by a thread

phrases.en: A slim chance still remains.
phrases.nuance_ko: 성공할 확률이 거의 없지만 완전히 없는 것은 아닐 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when the chance is tiny but not completely gone.

phrases.en: Our chance of winning is very slim.
phrases.nuance_ko: 해요체로 끝내서 상황을 바로 설명할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: The polite ending for stating the situation directly.

explain_en: It goes with things barely left, such as '희망' (hope), '가능성' (possibility) and '목숨' (life). It is easy to remember as the chunk '실낱같은 희망'.

t90.ax: His voice sounded as thin as a thread.

en: to be related; to be connected; to be linked

examples.ko: 이 사건은 지난달 일과 연관돼 있어요.
examples.en: This incident is connected to last month's event.
Health and sleep are deeply related.
I called in everyone involved and talked.
I don't want to be involved in that matter.
Check whether the two problems are connected.

examples.ko: 주제와 연관되지 않은 이야기는 빼 주세요.
examples.en: Please leave out stories unrelated to the topic.

explain: '관련되다'와 거의 같아서 바꿔 쓸 수 있어요. 조사는 '~와/과 연관되다'를 써요. 사건이나 사람이 어떤 일에 얽혀 있을 때도 쓰고, 이 경우에는 조금 부정적인 느낌이 날 수 있어요. 일상에서는 '관련이 있다'가 더 흔해요.

phrases.en: This problem is related to the environment.
phrases.nuance_ko: '연관되다'와 거의 같아서 바꿔 쓸 수 있고, 조금 더 일상적이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Nearly the same as '연관되다' and interchangeable, but a bit more everyday.

phrases.en: The two things are connected to each other.
phrases.nuance_ko: '연관되다'를 '~이 있다'로 풀어서 말하는 쉬운 형태예요.
phrases.nuance_en: An easier way to say it, using '~이 있다' instead of the verb form.

phrases.example: 그 사람은 그 사건과 연관되지 않았어요.
phrases.en: That person was not connected to the incident.
phrases.nuance_ko: 어떤 일에 얽히지 않았다고 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to say someone was not involved in something.

explain_en: Linked in a chain of connection, a bit more conceptual. Nearly interchangeable with '관련되다'. The pattern is '~와/과 연관되다'. When a person or event is tied up in some matter it can sound a bit negative. In daily talk '관련이 있다' is more common.

dis.h: linked in a chain of connection
gh: has to do with; concerns someone

p.n: Almost the same; 관련되다 is more general.

t90.ax: Health and sleep are deeply related.

en: to be gloomy; to be downcast

examples.ko: 시험에 떨어진 후로 그는 계속 침울해요.
examples.en: Ever since failing the exam, he has been gloomy.
My friend's expression looks gloomy today.
The meeting ended in a gloomy atmosphere.

examples.ko: 비 오는 날에는 마음이 침울해지곤 해요.
examples.en: On rainy days, my mood often turns gloomy.
Why are you sitting there looking so down?
My gloomy mood lifted thanks to my friend.

explain: '우울하다'는 마음 상태 전체에 쓰고, '침울하다'는 표정, 분위기, 목소리에 기운 없는 모습이 드러날 때 자주 써요. 사람뿐 아니라 '분위기'에도 쓸 수 있어요.

phrases.en: He came in with a gloomy expression.
phrases.nuance_ko: 기운 없는 얼굴이 보일 때 가장 자주 쓰는 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: This is the most common phrase for a face that looks low in energy.

phrases.example: 소식을 들은 뒤 방 안이 침울한 분위기였어요.
phrases.en: After hearing the news, the mood in the room was gloomy.
phrases.nuance_ko: 사람 한 명이 아니라 모임이나 장소 전체의 분위기를 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Use it for the mood of a whole group or place, not just one person.

phrases.en: My friend has been feeling down for several days.
phrases.nuance_ko: 다른 사람이 침울해하는 모습을 밖에서 보고 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Use it when describing someone else's gloomy state as you observe it.

explain_en: Low mood, heavy atmosphere after bad news — neutral to formal. '우울하다' covers the overall state of mind, while '침울하다' is often used when low spirits show in a face, atmosphere or voice. It can describe not only people but also a '분위기' (mood).

t90.ax: The meeting ended in a gloomy atmosphere.

examples.en: Don't rationalize your mistake; apologize first.
That's just rationalizing your laziness.

examples.ko: 자기 합리화가 심한 사람과는 대화하기 어려워요.
examples.en: It's hard to talk with someone who rationalizes their own actions a lot.

examples.ko: 회사는 업무 절차 합리화를 추진하고 있어요.
examples.en: The company is pushing to make its work procedures more rational.

examples.ko: 변명처럼 들리는 합리화는 누구나 해 본 적 있어요.
examples.en: Everyone has made rationalizations that sound like excuses.

examples.ko: 그 선택을 합리화할 이유를 찾고 있어요.
examples.en: I'm looking for a reason to justify that choice.

explain: 일상에서는 '자기 합리화'라는 말로 자주 써서, 잘못을 그럴듯한 이유로 덮는 안 좋은 느낌이 있어요. 반면 회사나 제도 이야기에서는 '절차를 합리화하다'처럼 더 효율적으로 바꾼다는 중립적인 뜻으로도 써요. 앞에 오는 말을 보고 구별해요.

phrases.en: That's nothing but self-justification.
phrases.nuance_ko: 자신의 잘못을 그럴듯하게 설명할 때 쓰는 가장 흔한 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The most common phrase for explaining away one's own fault.

phrases.en: Don't rationalize your own actions.
phrases.nuance_ko: 동사로 쓰면 잘못에 이유를 붙인다는 부정적인 느낌이 강해요.
phrases.nuance_en: As a verb it often has a negative feeling of making excuses.

phrases.en: The company made its work procedures more efficient.
phrases.nuance_ko: 제도나 방법을 더 효율적으로 바꾼다는 중립적인 뜻이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A neutral meaning of making a system or method more efficient.

explain_en: Making excuses for oneself, or making a process efficient. In daily talk it often appears as '자기 합리화' and has a negative feel of covering a fault with a plausible reason. In talk about companies or systems, as in '절차를 합리화하다', it is neutral and means making something more efficient. Look at the word before it to tell which one is meant.

examples.en: A ship checks its surroundings with radar.
A strange object showed up on the radar.

examples.ko: 공항 옆에 큰 레이더 한 대가 서 있어요.
examples.en: A large radar stands next to the airport.
Radar can also find rain clouds.

examples.ko: 레이더가 고장 나서 비행기가 늦게 떴어요.
examples.en: The radar broke, so the plane took off late.
Work to install a new radar has begun.

explain: '레이더에 잡히다'처럼 무언가가 발견될 때 말해요. 날씨 뉴스에서는 '기상 레이더'가 나와요.

phrases.en: A small boat showed up on the radar.
phrases.nuance_ko: 레이더로 무언가가 발견되었을 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when something is detected by radar.
phrases.en_equiv: to be picked up on radar

phrases.en: I check the rain clouds on the weather radar.
phrases.nuance_ko: 날씨를 살피는 레이더를 말할 때 앞에 '기상'을 붙여요.
phrases.nuance_en: Put 기상 before it for the radar that tracks weather.

phrases.en: The ship finds nearby ships using radar.
phrases.nuance_ko: '-(으)로'를 붙여 레이더를 도구로 쓴다는 뜻을 나타내요.
phrases.nuance_en: Adding -(으)로 shows that radar is the tool being used.

explain_en: It is used in '레이더에 잡히다' when something is detected. Weather news mentions '기상 레이더' (weather radar).

examples.en: The stitches in this embroidery are really delicate.
The stitches weren't even, so I sewed it again.
If you make the stitches small, the clothes are sturdier.
With hand sewing, care goes into every single stitch.

examples.ko: 바늘땀 사이가 너무 넓으면 금방 뜯어져요.
examples.en: If the gaps between stitches are too wide, it comes apart quickly.

examples.ko: 바늘땀이 보이지 않게 안쪽에서 꿰매 주세요.
examples.en: Please sew it from the inside so the stitches don't show.

explain: 바늘로 한 번 떠서 남은 자국 하나를 말해요. 줄여서 '땀'이라고도 하고, 손으로 정성껏 할 때 '한 땀 한 땀'이라고 말해요.

phrases.en: The stitches on this garment are tight, so it's sturdy.
phrases.nuance_ko: '바늘땀'을 줄인 말이에요. 몸에서 나는 '땀'과 소리는 같지만 뜻이 달라요.
phrases.nuance_en: A shortened form of 바늘땀. It sounds like 'sweat' (땀) but means something different.

phrases.example: 할머니가 한 땀 한 땀 수를 놓으셨어요.
phrases.en: Grandmother embroidered it one stitch at a time.
phrases.nuance_ko: 손으로 정성껏 천천히 할 때 쓰는 표현이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: An expression for doing handwork carefully, one stitch at a time.

phrases.example: 바늘땀이 촘촘해서 옷이 잘 안 뜯어져요.
phrases.en: The stitches are tight, so the clothes don't come apart easily.
phrases.nuance_ko: '촘촘하다, 고르다, 크다'처럼 바늘땀의 모양을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used with words like '촘촘하다' or '고르다' to describe how stitches look.

explain_en: It is the single mark left each time the needle goes through the cloth. People shorten it to '땀', and say '한 땀 한 땀' for careful hand work.

examples.en: This pot is made of stainless steel, so it's sturdy.

examples.ko: 스테인리스 컵은 오래 써도 냄새가 안 나요.
examples.en: A stainless steel cup doesn't smell even after long use.
A stainless steel kitchen sink is easy to clean.

examples.ko: 스테인리스 숟가락은 한국 식당에서 흔히 볼 수 있어요.
examples.en: Stainless steel spoons are commonly seen in Korean restaurants.

examples.ko: 저는 플라스틱 대신 스테인리스 빨대를 써요.
examples.en: I use stainless steel straws instead of plastic.
Stainless steel doesn't rust easily.

explain: '스테인리스'는 녹이 잘 슬지 않는 금속이에요. 한국 식당의 젓가락, 숟가락, 물컵이 대부분 스테인리스라서 일상에서 아주 자주 보이는 소재예요. 줄여서 '스뎅'이라고도 하는데 이건 일상 대화에서만 써요.

phrases.en: I like the stainless bowl because it's light.
phrases.nuance_ko: '스테인리스'를 편하게 부르는 말이에요. 친구나 가족끼리 말할 때만 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: A casual way to say 스테인리스, used only in everyday talk.

phrases.en: The restaurant gave me a stainless steel spoon.
phrases.nuance_ko: 한국 식당에서 흔히 보는 물건과 함께 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Pairs with items commonly seen in Korean restaurants.

phrases.en: This bottle is made of stainless steel, so it's sturdy.
phrases.nuance_ko: 물건이 어떤 소재인지 설명할 때 '재질'과 같이 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used with 재질 to explain what a thing is made of.

explain_en: 스테인리스 is a metal that does not rust easily. Chopsticks, spoons, and cups in Korean restaurants are mostly stainless steel, so it is a very common everyday material. People also say 스뎅 in casual talk, but only in conversation.

examples.en: The delivery box was full of styrofoam.
Styrofoam is thrown away separately.
The fish box is made of styrofoam, so it's light.
I got hot coffee in a styrofoam cup.
My child made a boat out of styrofoam.
Bits of styrofoam were scattered on the floor.

explain: 원래 상품 이름에서 왔지만 지금은 흰색 발포 플라스틱을 두루 부르는 말이에요. 포장 상자나 일회용 컵 이야기에서 자주 나와요.

phrases.en: The fish came packed in a styrofoam box.
phrases.nuance_ko: 포장이나 배달 이야기에서 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Common when talking about packaging or delivery.

phrases.en: I throw styrofoam in the recycling bin.
phrases.nuance_ko: 분리배출 이야기에서 자주 쓰는 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A common pairing when talking about recycling.

phrases.example: 스티로폼 컵에 따뜻한 커피를 담아 줬어요.
phrases.en: They gave me hot coffee in a styrofoam cup.
phrases.nuance_ko: 일회용 컵을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for disposable cups.

explain_en: It started as a product name but now generally refers to white foam plastic. It often comes up when talking about packing boxes or disposable cups.

examples.ko: 산속에 작은 오두막이 한 채 있어요.
examples.en: There is one small hut in the mountains.
It rained, so we went inside the hut.
Grandfather lives alone in a hut in the forest.
We built a fire in front of the hut.
Though the hut was shabby, it was warm in winter.

examples.ko: 나무로 직접 오두막을 지어 보고 싶어요.
examples.en: I want to build a hut myself out of wood.

explain: 작고 허름하게 지은 집을 말해서 '펜션'이나 '별장'처럼 깔끔한 느낌은 없어요. 산이나 숲, 바닷가에 있는 단순한 집에 써요. 동화나 이야기에 자주 나오는 말이에요.

phrases.en: There is a small hut in the forest.
phrases.nuance_ko: 오두막이 작고 소박하다는 느낌을 더하는 자연스러운 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A natural pairing that stresses the hut is small and simple.

phrases.en: My grandfather lives in a hut in the mountains.
phrases.nuance_ko: 장소를 앞에 붙여 오두막이 어디에 있는지 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Putting the place first tells where the hut is.

phrases.en: Long ago, an old man lived in a hut.
phrases.nuance_ko: 이야기나 동화에서 자주 쓰는 표현이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Often used in stories and fairy tales.

explain_en: Small simple hut as a dwelling, e.g., in mountains (산속 오두막) It means a small, rough house, so it lacks the tidy feel of 펜션 or 별장. It fits a simple home in the mountains, forest or by the sea. It often appears in fairy tales and stories.

examples.en: There is a spring inside the ballpoint pen.
The bed spring is broken and makes a noise.
I sprang up like a spring and caught the ball.
The child rolled a spring toy down the stairs.
If you press the spring hard, it pops back out.
The springs inside the mattress are old and have stretched.

explain: '스프링'이라고도 말해요. 볼펜, 침대, 장난감처럼 눌렀다 놓으면 되돌아오는 부품에 써요. '용수철 장난감'처럼 다른 명사 앞에 붙여 쓰기도 해요.

phrases.en: The chair's spring is broken.
phrases.nuance_ko: 영어에서 온 말로, 일상에서 '용수철' 대신 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: An English-origin word often used in daily speech instead of '용수철'.

phrases.en: The child likes spring toys.
phrases.nuance_ko: 다른 명사 앞에 붙여서 쓰는 형태예요.
phrases.nuance_en: Placed before another noun to describe it.

phrases.en: If you pull it by hand, the spring stretches.
phrases.nuance_ko: 용수철의 성질을 설명할 때 쓰는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to explain how a spring behaves.

explain_en: People also say '스프링'. It is used for parts that return to shape after being pressed, like in pens, beds and toys. It can also go before another noun, as in '용수철 장난감'.

t90.ax: There is a spring inside the ballpoint pen.

en: to be small; to be narrow; to be cramped

examples.ko: 우리 집은 주방이 협소해서 요리하기 불편해요.
examples.en: Our kitchen is cramped, so it's inconvenient to cook.

examples.ko: 협소한 공간에서도 쓸 수 있는 접이식 책상을 샀어요.
examples.en: I bought a folding desk that can be used even in a tight space.

examples.ko: 가게가 너무 협소하면 손님이 오래 머물기 어려워요.
examples.en: If a shop is too cramped, it's hard for customers to stay long.
The parking lot is small, so please use public transportation.

examples.ko: 직원이 늘어서 사무실이 협소해졌다고 다들 말해요.
examples.en: Everyone says the office has become cramped because we hired more people.

examples.ko: 이 방은 협소하지만 햇빛이 잘 들어서 좋아요.
examples.en: This room is small, but I like it because it gets a lot of sunlight.

explain: '좁다'와 비슷하지만 '협소하다'는 공간이나 면적이 좁아서 불편하다는 말을 정중하게 할 때 써요. 안내문이나 부동산, 뉴스에서 잘 어울려요. 옷이 좁거나 마음이 좁을 때는 '좁다'를 쓰고, 반대말은 '넓다'예요.

phrases.example: 협소한 주차장이라 큰 차는 들어가기 어려워요.
phrases.en: It is a cramped parking lot, so big cars have trouble getting in.
phrases.nuance_ko: '협소한 + 장소'로 좁은 공간을 정중하게 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: '협소한 + place' politely describes a cramped space.

phrases.en: This office is not as cramped as I thought.
phrases.nuance_ko: 생각보다 충분히 넓다는 뜻으로 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Says the space is roomy enough.

phrases.example: 가게 공간이 협소해서 손님을 많이 받기 어려워요.
phrases.en: The shop space is cramped, so it is hard to take many customers.
phrases.nuance_ko: '공간이 협소해서'로 이유를 말할 때 많이 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: '공간이 협소해서' is often used to give a reason.

explain_en: It is similar to '좁다', but '협소하다' is used to say politely or formally that a space or area is too small to be comfortable. It fits notices, real estate and the news. For tight clothes or a narrow mind, use '좁다'; the opposite is '넓다'.

dis.h: formal; too narrow or cramped space

p.n: 협소하다 stresses lack of space and is formal; 작다 only says small.

t90.ax: Our kitchen is cramped, so it's inconvenient to cook.
